name: Zephyra Brasscoil
equipment: Cinderweave Cloak (resistance to fire damage — layered atop innate tiefling resistance)
Arcane focus (a brass dragon-scale amulet, warm to the touch)
A set of weighted dice and marked cards
A forged writ of passage stamped with a City-of-Brass seal

weapons.name: Chromatic Orb (ranged spell attack, choose damage type)

features: Dragon Ancestor (Brass; can speak and understand Draconic, double proficiency on Cha checks with dragons)
Draconic Resilience (+1 HP per sorcerer level; AC = 13 + Dex mod when unarmored)
Elemental Affinity (add Charisma modifier to one fire damage roll; spend 1 sorcery point for fire resistance for 1 hour)
Font of Magic (9 sorcery points; convert between sorcery points and spell slots)
Metamagic: Quickened Spell, Twinned Spell, Empowered Spell
Infernal Legacy (Thaumaturgy cantrip; Hellish Rebuke at 2nd level and Darkness, each once per long rest, Cha-based)
traits: Doubly fire-resistant (tiefling Hellish Resistance plus Elemental Affinity), but leans on force, cold, and lightning against fire-immune foes
Silver-tongued grifter who talks her way past bindings and bargains alike

personality.traits: I could sell a salamander a scarf. Every locked door is just a conversation I haven't had yet.
personality.ideals: Freedom. Bindings, contracts, and cages exist to be slipped — especially the efreeti kind.
personality.bonds: The brass warmth in my blood is my one honest thing; I'd cross a plane of fire to learn where it came from.
personality.flaws: I bluff first and think second, and my mouth has written checks my spell slots can't always cash.

appearance: A striking tiefling with burnished brass-gold skin, curling horns filed to a polished sheen, and eyes like molten amber. A faint metallic shimmer runs along her jaw and knuckles — the mark of her draconic line. She dresses in scavenged finery, all confidence and misdirection, her dragon-scale amulet always warm against her sternum.
backstory: Zephyra grew up running cons in a portside city, never quite fitting the infernal story her horns told — her magic answered to brass, not brimstone, and warmth pooled in her chest whenever she lied well. She was mid-swindle when the Emberscar opened over the harbor, and in the chaos she saw an opportunity too grand to pass up: a forged writ, a place among the Ashen Vow's expedition, and a free ride to the one city that might explain the dragon in her blood. She signed on as the party's face, telling herself it was just another job — and only half believing it.
